recipes.name: Crab Alfredo
ingredients_raw: salt and black pepper to taste

steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook for 8 to 10 minutes or until al dente; drain. Keep warm and covered.

Meanwhile, melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and cook until garlic releases its aroma, about 2 minutes, being careful not to let the garlic brown. Stir in the flour, salt, pepper, and cayenne pepper. Reduce heat, and cook, stirring constantly for about 2 minutes. Add the half-and-half and stir over medium heat until slightly thickened, about 3 minutes.
Add the cream cheese and Parmesan cheese to the sauce and stir until cheeses melt and mixture is smooth. Mix in the crabmeat and continue cooking until crabmeat is heated through, about 3 minutes.
Divide the fettucine between 2 plates or bowls and top with the crab sauce.

raw_recipe.headline: Crab Alfredo
raw_recipe.description: Simply put, delicious! A little on the decadent side, but it can be made with fat-free half-and-half and a heart-healthy spread instead of butter. Serve with garlic bread sticks, a nice salad, and a glass of Chardonnay.

review.reviewBody: I have been looking for and testing different Alfredo Sauce recipes at home and at every restuarant out there. Thanks for this one. It is by far the best I've ever eaten and so easy to make. I did use the conversion to 2% milk because it's all I had in the house (7/8 cup milk plus 1 tablespoon butter). It still came out rich and thick. I left out the cayenne because i don't like the heat and added instead somewhere between 1/4-1/2 tsp of nutmeg, which all true alfredo sauce recipes call fo,r and that put it OVER THE TOP!! I confess I also added a little extra grated and schredded cheese because let's face it, you can never have too much cheese! The more I added, the better it tasted. I have also tried this sauce with chicken and broccoli instead of crab which was also very good. I will use this as a base for any recipe calling for an alfredo sauce in the future. My search is over!! THANKS AGAIN!!!!!

This is a good recipe, but I changed it up a little, and it was very good. I sautéed 1/4 Cup chopped onion with the garlic I used 1 Cup of heavy cream and 4 Tbs of sour cream instead of 1/2 and 1/2. I also used 8 oz of cream cheese versus 4, used Tabasco versus cayenne, and added 2 oz. of dry sherry. I also used 2 containers of crab instead of of one. I know it sounds like I changed it alot, but most of it was because I prefer Tabasco to cayenne and had 2 containers of crab. That's what drove most of the changes. Plus, being from the south, I really like adding sherry to crab recipes (e.g., she-crab soup). This will also make a very good hot crab dip.

Delicious! Just like Red Lobster! I made it a bit lighter by using low fat cream cheese and also 1% milk instead of cream (but I added just a bit more butter.) At first when you are stirring it, the mix looks like it's all lumpy and it won't work - but then eventually it all comes together nicely. I did whisk it with a fork to get any flour lumps out. Use the shredded Parmesan cheese in the plastic tub that you get in the deli section for some stringiness to the sauce. I'm sure you can go Gluten Free on this recipe and skip the flour - it can thicken up on it's own without it. I didn't measure the cayenne, so I ended up putting a bit too much in (hubby loved it, kids thought it was a tad spicy, but not bad) so to tone it down I added fresh chopped spinach and some chopped tomatoes. I must say - the colors of the spinach and tomato really made it pop! Added a little healthy flair to boot. The whole family loved it and thought it was DELICIOUS. Also threw in some left over shrimp - great dish! Kids were 10 and 12 and gobbled it right up.

My edits:
1. Used 1% milk instead of half and half
2. Used low fat cream cheese
3. Added a bit more butter
4. Used 2x the garlic
4. Added shrimp
5. Added chopped fresh spinach and fresh tomato
6. Used linguine

After everything cooked, I poured all the pasta in a bowl and poured the sauce on top and tossed well so the pasta was coated.

I'm thinking mushrooms and/or peas would also go well in the dish.

Enjoy!

I'm a 16 year old guy and I made this dish for my family and I have to say, it's delicious! The sauce had the perfect consistency when I added 1/3 cup of milk in addition to the half and half. I added extra garlic and cayenne pepper seasoning because we like our food more spicy. The addition of about a teaspoon of Old Bay seasoning put it over the top. If you have family coming over, this is the perfect recipe!

I made this dairy free. I used almond milk instead of half and half, margarine, vegan Parmesan and vegan mozzarella for the cream cheese. I thought I had vegan cream cheese and it was sour cream so I had to think fast. I used nutmeg instead of cayenne and used broccoli and chicken instead of crab. I also used whole wheat penne. It was great. Next time I will used the crab meat and cream cheese. It was and easy dairy free meal.

I've made this delicious recipe twice now. I gave 4 stars only because I made several changes. The changes were primarily for health reasons. I used olive oil in place of butter and reduced-fat cream cheese (neufchatel) as well as fat-free half & half. I significantly increased the garlic & omitted the cayenne pepper as personal preferences and omitted the salt because I follow a low sodium diet. I also used chicken and added broccoli. I will definitely be making this regularly.

We didn't have half and half, so we mixed one and half cups of milk and 1/2 cup of butter. Also cut the cayenne as other reviewers suggested. We used fresh crab leg meat. This is definitely NOT a delicate meal, it's extremely hearty and fattening, but OH SO worth it!!!! It is perfectly thick, I like a nice thick sauce. We separated the crab so it was just in the dish we ate that night. The left overs in the fridge the next day were solid, but melted right back down in the microwave and was still just as good as the night before, even without the crab...I couldn't get enough!

This is a lovely sauce! I had a 16-oz can of good-quality crabmeat so I doubled everything here except the cayenne pepper. At 1/2 tsp it was still plenty! I used butter and half & half, so added Neufchâtel cream cheese to cut the calories just a bit. Had already used up my block of Parmesan cheese, but had a very firm wedge of aged Gouda and it worked quite well. Will try this again when I next need Alfredo sauce.
I just made the sauce and it was delicious!!! I did thin it out with a bit of milk and skipped the cream cheese because I didn't have any. It didn't need it - YUM!
Used skim milk and only 1/4 tsp of cayenne - my son loved it!
This was a great recipe it was quick and very rewarding I used more crab meat and a little more parmesan cheese. It was a hit with the whole family
Amazing seriously we added extra parm, pepper and nutmeg it was freaking amazing!!!!
Sooo good! I would t add or change anything

Made this recipe with a few changes. Used 1 percent milk and only two tablespoons flour and the consistency of the sauce was perfect for us, rich but not cloying. We loved this recipe and could see using it with chicken, shrimp, salmon or a vegetable pasta etc. Definitely will be making again.
Made as is and it was excellent. Son said it was the best Alfredo he has ever had. I use this for chicken & shrimp as well PERFECT!
I added shrimp to my pasta. Turned out great
Loved it! I would cut the cayenne in half, leave out the cream cheese and add more half&half (or use whole milk) .This recipe is AMAZING.
was awesome, we just added spinach aswell, my husband said he preferred this over my regular chicken alfredo so i will be making this again
